newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's outlawed union body postpones strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's outlawed union body postpones strike.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed union body will postpone a four-hour nationwide strike threatened for Friday in protest at proposed changes to the labour law, a union spokesman said.

"We have decided to postpone the earlier plan because we believe there is little chance that the law will be passed by parliament," Yoon Young-mo, a spokesman for the Korea Confederation of Trade Unions told Reuters.

On Thursday, opposition parties called for a delay in pushing through a new labour bill that allows layoffs and flexible work hours. The ruling New Korea Party wants to adopt the bill during the current session of parliament, which ends on December 18.
Yoon said the disagreement on timing meant it was unlikely the bill would become law before parliament breaks up.
The confederation, which claims a membership of 500,000 in 300 companies, had called for the strike to begin at 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT). It also planned an indefinite walkout on Monday.

Its larger counterpart, the more conservative Korea Federation of Trade Unions, said it would call out its union affiliates for one hour on Monday and three hours on Thursday. There was no immediate word on its latest intentions.

The New Korea Party appealed to the union bodies on Thursday to drop plans for industrial action, saying it was "sympathetic" to labour but it was impossible to change the law and satisfy workers and managers.
